weeks.theme: Set the shared working language and collaboration norms

scenarios.title: Agree on the integration standup ground rules
scenarios.situation: Kick off the merged team's daily standup across KR/JP time zones and tools.
targetPhrases: Let's capture this in the working agreement.
scenarios.successLooksLike: We end with a 1-page working agreement (time, channel, length, roles) everyone understands and follows the next day.

scenarios.title: Write a purpose-driven meeting agenda
scenarios.situation: Schedule a cross-functional planning session with PM, Eng, Ops from both companies.
targetPhrases: By the end of this meeting we will…
scenarios.successLooksLike: Invites include a clear objective, timebox, decision maker, and attendees come prepared; meeting finishes on time with decisions recorded.

scenarios.title: Clarify acronyms and terminology politely
scenarios.situation: Two tools and vocabularies collide; avoid misunderstandings.
targetPhrases: Just to confirm, when you say X, do you mean…?
Could we align on terminology for…?
Let's document this term in the glossary.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Misunderstandings are surfaced and resolved quickly; a shared glossary is started and linked in the channel.

weeks.theme: Crisp status, clear asks, and reliable handoffs

scenarios.title: Deliver a 60–90 second status update
scenarios.situation: Daily standup across KR/JP with execs occasionally listening in.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Updates are under 90 seconds, include progress, next step, blocker, and a specific request; blockers are resolved faster.

scenarios.title: Write a timezone handoff note
scenarios.situation: Pass work between JST and KST without meetings.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Receiving teammate can continue work without pinging for basics; errors drop and cycle time improves.

scenarios.title: Ask for help and set expectations
scenarios.situation: You need another team to pick up a task with a clear deadline.
targetPhrases: Could you take this by EOD KST/JST?
If not, who is the right owner?
What do you need from me to proceed?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Requests get accepted or redirected within the day, with clear owners and deadlines recorded.

weeks.theme: Merge roadmaps and make work executable

scenarios.title: Prioritize and merge two backlogs
scenarios.situation: Combine overlapping features and conflicting priorities.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Top 10 items are agreed with rationale and captured; duplicate work is removed.

scenarios.title: Write a Jira ticket with strong acceptance criteria
scenarios.situation: Ensure another squad can build/test without meetings.
scenarios.successLooksLike: A peer can implement and test using only the ticket; few clarification pings.

scenarios.title: Define RACI for a workstream
scenarios.situation: Ambiguity over who decides and who informs.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Names are assigned to R/A/C/I; decisions speed up and escalations follow the agreed path.

scenarios.title: Clarify an ambiguous requirement
scenarios.situation: PM request is unclear to Eng/Ops.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Team agrees on the user problem and success metrics; unknowns are tracked with owners.

scenarios.title: Propose and agree an API contract change
scenarios.situation: Two services must integrate without breaking clients.
scenarios.successLooksLike: A versioned plan and timeline are accepted; change is documented and shared to all consumers.

scenarios.title: Raise a dependency risk early
scenarios.situation: Another team’s delay threatens your milestone.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Risk is logged with owners and dates; leadership understands impact and options.

scenarios.title: Run a joint architecture review
scenarios.situation: Choose an approach that balances both systems’ strengths.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Decision and rationale are clear; follow-up actions and owners are recorded in an ADR.

scenarios.title: Plan a safe data migration
scenarios.situation: Unify databases with minimal downtime.
scenarios.successLooksLike: A migration plan exists with timings, validation steps, and rollback; stakeholders sign off.

scenarios.title: Write a concise decision memo (ADR)
scenarios.situation: Summarize context, options, decision, and consequences.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Leaders skim once and understand; no follow-up meeting needed to clarify the decision.

scenarios.title: Align on QA definitions
scenarios.situation: Two teams use different DoR/DoD and severity scales.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Shared DoR/DoD and severity definitions are adopted and referenced in tickets.

scenarios.title: Create a unified release plan
scenarios.situation: Coordinate releases across services and regions.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Release calendar is agreed; changes land predictably with fewer hotfixes.

scenarios.title: Run a UAT go/no-go meeting
scenarios.situation: Decide if the release is ready.
scenarios.successLooksLike: A clear go/no-go decision is made in the meeting with sign-offs and next steps.

scenarios.title: Escalate and staff an incident fast
scenarios.situation: Production issue impacts customers during integration.
targetPhrases: Need an IC and a comms lead
scenarios.successLooksLike: Within minutes, roles are assigned, bridge is active, and impact/next steps are posted in the channel.

scenarios.title: Write a clean incident timeline
scenarios.situation: Document events for stakeholders and learning.
scenarios.successLooksLike: A single timeline replaces scattered chats; leadership can brief customers with confidence.

scenarios.title: Lead a blameless postmortem
scenarios.situation: Turn an outage into improvements without finger-pointing.
scenarios.successLooksLike: We leave with 3–5 systemic actions, owners, and dates; no personal blame in notes.

scenarios.title: Draft a customer-facing change notice
scenarios.situation: Notify enterprise customers about product changes.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Email is clear, jargon-free, and approved by legal/support on first pass.

scenarios.title: De-escalate a transferred customer
scenarios.situation: A frustrated customer has been routed multiple times.
targetPhrases: I understand you've repeated this already.
Here's what will happen in the next 15 minutes…
scenarios.successLooksLike: Customer calms down, gets a clear next step and timeline, and stays on the line to resolution.

scenarios.title: Write an executive weekly update
scenarios.situation: Brief KR/JP leadership on progress and risks.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Leaders can skim one paragraph and know status, risks, and what you need from them.

weeks.theme: Vendors, security, and compliance in a merger

scenarios.title: Answer audit and security questions
scenarios.situation: Respond to ISO/ISMS/SOC evidence requests.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Auditors get precise answers with links; fewer back-and-forth emails.

scenarios.title: Negotiate vendor consolidation
scenarios.situation: Choose one tool and plan migration.
scenarios.successLooksLike: A shortlist, pilot plan, and timeline are agreed; costs and risks are visible.

scenarios.title: Handle cross-border data privacy
scenarios.situation: KR/JP data rules differ; align practices.
scenarios.successLooksLike: A compliant approach is documented and approved by legal and security.

scenarios.title: Align on KPIs and OKRs
scenarios.situation: Create shared goals that drive the integration.
scenarios.successLooksLike: A small set of KPIs/OKRs is published with owners and review cadence.

scenarios.title: Negotiate SLAs across teams
scenarios.situation: Set realistic uptime and response targets.
scenarios.successLooksLike: SLA terms are agreed and documented; monitoring aligns to targets.

scenarios.title: Write a dashboard requirement brief
scenarios.situation: Specify what leaders need to see to make decisions.
scenarios.successLooksLike: BI can build without follow-ups; the dashboard supports weekly decisions.

scenarios.title: Run the war room run-of-show
scenarios.situation: Coordinate roles, cadence, and updates during cutover.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Everyone knows their role; updates and decisions are posted on schedule.

scenarios.title: Make real-time decisions under pressure
scenarios.situation: Timeboxed calls during incidents or cutover.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Decisions are made quickly, recorded, and owned; no circular debate.

scenarios.title: Triage issues fast and fairly
scenarios.situation: Sort new issues and assign to the right squads.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Issues are categorized and assigned within minutes; ETAs are communicated.

weeks.theme: Retrospective, handover, and sustaining ways of working

scenarios.title: Run a cross-team retrospective
scenarios.situation: Close the integration phase and capture learnings.
scenarios.successLooksLike: We leave with 5 prioritized improvements and owners; sentiment is positive and forward-looking.

scenarios.title: Handover to business-as-usual
scenarios.situation: Transition responsibilities to steady-state teams.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Handover is accepted without gaps; on-call and ownership are unambiguous.

scenarios.title: Write the closure email and next steps
scenarios.situation: Announce outcomes and what's next to all stakeholders.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Stakeholders understand outcomes and who owns what; no confusion after the announcement.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Team members give a focused 60–90 second update that states progress, next step, blocker, and a specific ask.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: In a timed role-play, participants include all 4 elements and finish under 90 seconds in 2 of 3 rounds.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Cross-timezone handoffs are clear enough that the next person can proceed without a call.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: In a writing task, 80% of peers can start work using only the note; rubric score ≥4/5 on context, next step, owner, due time.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Tickets include acceptance criteria and definitions so another team can build and test without clarification.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: Given a scenario, learners produce a ticket with Given/When/Then, dependencies, and DoD; 4 of 5 checklist items met.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: People can run a 15-minute decision meeting to a clear decision with owners and deadlines.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: In a facilitation role-play, the objective, timebox, options, decision, and owners are all stated; 4 of 5 elements present.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: During an incident, messages are concise, factual, and assign actions immediately.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: In a drill, the initial announcement includes severity, impact, ask, and channel within 2 minutes; 3 of 4 elements present.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Leaders receive one-paragraph weekly updates that are clear, jargon-free, and highlight risks and asks.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: Written update scores ≥4/5 on clarity, brevity, jargon removal, explicit risks, and explicit asks on a rubric.

kickoffMessage.en: Welcome! Two strong teams from Korea and Japan are becoming one. Our shared working language will be English so we can move fast together. Over the next 12 weeks we’ll practice exactly what you need for a smooth merger: running crisp standups, writing handoffs and Jira tickets, aligning roadmaps and SLAs, resolving dependencies, handling incidents, and communicating clearly with customers and executives. Expect two 75‑minute live sessions per week plus short applied tasks using your real materials (tickets, emails, updates). This is a safe room: we value clarity over perfect grammar, and we’ll build simple phrases you can use immediately. Let’s respect both cultures, be direct and kind, and make decisions visible. Success means you can run a meeting, write a handoff, and get to a decision without switching languages. Let’s get started.
kickoffMessage.ko: 환영합니다! 한국과 일본의 두 강한 팀이 하나로 합쳐집니다. 우리 팀의 공용 업무 언어는 English(영어)입니다. 앞으로 12주 동안 실제 통합에 꼭 필요한 상황을 집중적으로 연습합니다: 간결한 스탠드업 진행, 시간대 간 핸드오프와 Jira 티켓 작성, 로드맵·SLA 정렬, 의존성 조정, 인시던트 대응, 그리고 고객·경영진과의 명확한 커뮤니케이션 등입니다. 주 2회 75분 라이브 세션과 짧은 실습 과제가 있으며, 실제 자료(티켓, 이메일, 주간 업데이트)를 사용합니다. 이 공간은 안전한 학습 환경입니다. 완벽한 문법보다 ‘명확한 전달’을 우선하며, 바로 쓸 수 있는 간단한 표현을 함께 만듭니다. 서로의 문화를 존중하고, 직설적이되 친절하게 소통하며, 결정 사항을 모두가 볼 수 있게 기록하겠습니다. 목표는 회의를 주도하고, 핸드오프를 쓰고, 언어 전환 없이 결정을 이끌어낼 수 있게 되는 것입니다. 지금 시작합시다!
